questions.question_english: Article 15(5) of the Constitution of India empowers the State to make special provisions regarding admission to educational institutions. Which Constitutional Amendment inserted this clause?
options_english: 77th Amendment Act, 1995
85th Amendment Act, 2001
93rd Amendment Act, 2005
103rd Amendment Act, 2019
questions.explanation_english: Article 15(5) was inserted into the Constitution of India by the Constitution (Ninety-Third Amendment) Act, 2005, which took effect on 20 January 2006. Parliament introduced this amendment to counteract the judicial rulings in T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka (2002) and P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra (2005), where the Supreme Court had ruled that the State could not impose reservation quotas on private unaided educational institutions. Clause (5) of Article 15 expressly authorizes the State to make special provisions by law for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes of citizens (SEBCs) or for the SCs and STs regarding admission to educational institutions, including private institutions (whether aided or unaided by the State), excluding only minority institutions referred to in Article 30(1).
questions.explanation_hindi: भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 15(5) संविधान (93वां संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2005 द्वारा अंतःस्थापित किया गया था, जो 20 जनवरी 2006 से प्रभावी हुआ। संसद ने यह संशोधन सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के 'टी.एम.ए. पाई फाउंडेशन बनाम कर्नाटक राज्य (2002)' और 'पी.ए. इनामदार बनाम महाराष्ट्र राज्य (2005)' के निर्णयों के प्रभाव को समाप्त करने के लिए किया था, जिनमें न्यायालय ने यह व्यवस्था दी थी कि राज्य निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त शिक्षण संस्थानों पर आरक्षण कोटा लागू नहीं कर सकता। अनुच्छेद 15(5) राज्य को कानून बनाकर सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों (SEBCs) अथवा अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लिए निजी शैक्षणिक संस्थानों (सहायता प्राप्त या गैर-सहायता प्राप्त दोनों) में प्रवेश हेतु विशेष प्रावधान करने का अधिकार देता है, केवल अनुच्छेद 30(1) के तहत स्थापित अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों को छोड़कर।

questions.question_english: Under the POSH Act, 2013, if the employer himself is accused of workplace sexual harassment, where should the aggrieved woman submit her formal complaint?
options_english: Internal Complaints Committee (ICC / IC)
Local Complaints Committee (LCC / LC)
Labour Court
Directly to the High Court
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 6(1) of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act), every District Officer is required to constitute a Local Committee (formerly known as the Local Complaints Committee or LCC) in each district. The statute specifically mandates that where an establishment has fewer than 10 workers or where the complaint of sexual harassment is against the employer himself, the aggrieved woman must file her complaint directly with the Local Committee. The Internal Complaints Committee (ICC/IC) cannot inquire into allegations against the employer because the employer exercises administrative and financial control over the workplace and the ICC members, creating an unavoidable conflict of interest and violating the fundamental principle of natural justice ('nemo judex in causa sua' — no one should be a judge in their own cause). In the context of school administration, if allegations are leveled against the school owner, manager, or head of the managing committee/trust who acts as the legal employer, the matter falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of the district Local Committee.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर B (स्थानीय शिकायत समिति - LCC / LC) है।

कार्यस्थल पर महिलाओं का लैंगिक उत्पीड़न (रोकथाम, प्रतिषेध एवं निवारण) अधिनियम (POSH Act), 2013 की धारा 6(1) के तहत प्रत्येक जिला अधिकारी (District Officer) द्वारा प्रत्येक जिले में एक 'स्थानीय समिति' (जिसे पूर्व में स्थानीय शिकायत समिति या LCC कहा जाता था) का गठन करना अनिवार्य है।

धारा 6(1) स्पष्ट रूप से यह प्रावधान करती है कि:
1. यदि किसी कार्यस्थल पर कर्मचारियों की संख्या 10 से कम होने के कारण आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) का गठन नहीं हुआ है, अथवा
2. यदि लैंगिक उत्पीड़न की शिकायत स्वयं 'नियोक्ता' (Employer) के विरुद्ध है,
तो व्यथित महिला अपनी शिकायत सीधे जिला स्तर पर गठित स्थानीय शिकायत समिति (LCC) के समक्ष प्रस्तुत करेगी।

आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) नियोक्ता के अधीन कार्यरत कर्मियों से मिलकर बनती है। अतः यदि शिकायत स्वयं नियोक्ता के विरुद्ध हो, तो नैसर्गिक न्याय के सिद्धांत ('कोई भी व्यक्ति अपने ही मामले में न्यायाधीश नहीं हो सकता') के तहत हितों का टकराव (Conflict of Interest) उत्पन्न होता है। विद्यालय प्रबंधन में यदि स्कूल प्रबंधक, ट्रस्टी या संस्था प्रमुख (जो नियोक्ता की श्रेणी में आते हैं) के विरुद्ध आरोप हो, तो जांच LCC द्वारा ही की जाती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Local Complaints Committee (LCC)

questions.question_english: According to the official criteria notified by the Government of India for determining eligibility under the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) quota, what is the maximum gross annual family income threshold?
options_english: Rs. 5.00 Lakhs
Rs. 6.00 Lakhs
Rs. 8.00 Lakhs

questions.explanation_english:
Under Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) Office Memorandum No. 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) dated 31 January 2019, the Central Government established the criteria for determining Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).

Para 4.1 of the OM specifies that persons whose family has a 'gross annual income below Rs. 8.00 lakh (Rupees eight lakh only)' are to be identified as EWS for the benefit of reservation. 

Key aspects of the income criteria include:
1. The income threshold covers all revenue sources: salary, agriculture, business, profession, interest, dividends, etc.
2. The relevant period is the financial year prior to the year of application for the EWS Income and Asset Certificate.
3. 'Family' for this purpose includes the person who seeks the benefit of reservation, his/her parents and siblings below the age of 18 years, as well as his/her spouse and children below the age of 18 years.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कार्मिक एवं प्रशिक्षण विभाग (DoPT), भारत सरकार के कार्यालय ज्ञापन संख्या 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) दिनांक 31 जनवरी 2019 के अनुसार, आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग (EWS) के निर्धारण हेतु आय मानदंड स्थापित किए गए हैं।

इस ज्ञापन के पैरा 4.1 के अनुसार, जिस परिवार की सकल वार्षिक आय ₹8.00 लाख (आठ लाख रुपये) से कम है, उसे आरक्षण के प्रयोजन के लिए EWS के रूप में चिह्नित किया जाएगा।

इस मानदंड की मुख्य विशेषताएं निम्न हैं:
1. इस आय में सभी स्रोतों से प्राप्त आय सम्मिलित है: वेतन, कृषि, व्यवसाय, पेशा आदि।
2. आय की गणना आवेदन वर्ष से ठीक पूर्ववर्ती वित्तीय वर्ष (financial year prior to application) के आधार पर की जाती है।
3. 'परिवार' में आवेदक, उसके माता-पिता, 18 वर्ष से कम आयु के भाई-बहन, जीवनसाथी तथा 18 वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चे शामिल होते हैं।

questions.question_english: What central constitutional argument did the Supreme Court accept in Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India concerning the 25% EWS quota?
options_english: Reasonable restrictions under Article 19(6), in the public interest served by Article 21A, can support the quota for covered private unaided schools.

questions.explanation_english:
Section 4(4) of the POSH Act, 2013 explicitly prescribes the tenure of the Internal Complaints Committee members:
'The Presiding Officer and every Member of the Internal Committee shall hold office for such period, not exceeding three years, from the date of their nomination as may be specified by the employer.'

Key Statutory and Administrative Points:
1. Statutory Ceiling: While an employer or school management may specify a shorter tenure (e.g., one or two years) upon nomination, the statutory ceiling is strictly three years.
2. Disqualification/Removal: Under Section 4(5), members may be removed prior to the expiration of their three-year tenure if they breach confidentiality (Section 16), face criminal conviction, are found guilty of departmental misconduct, or abuse their position.
3. Institutional Reconstitution: Employers must timely reconstitute or re-nominate the ICC upon the completion of this three-year maximum term to prevent legal challenges to inquiry proceedings.

Thus, the maximum tenure is 3 years (Option C).

questions.question_english: If a reserved vacancy in a teaching or administrative post cannot be filled due to the non-availability of an eligible candidate from the respective reserved category, the formal process of lifting the reservation restriction to fill it with an unreserved candidate is termed as:
options_english: Derecognition
De-reservation
Generalization
Re-appropriation
questions.explanation_english: In government service and educational administration, the formal procedure of removing the reservation tag from a reserved vacancy to enable the appointment of an unreserved/general candidate is officially termed 'De-reservation' (वि-आरक्षण). Under current DoPT rules and government policy, there is a general ban on de-reservation in direct recruitment posts; unfilled reserved vacancies must ordinarily be re-advertised and carried forward as 'backlog vacancies'. De-reservation in direct recruitment is permissible only in exceptionally rare and unavoidable circumstances in public interest, requiring prior concurrence from the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) and consultation with the relevant National Commission (NCSC, NCST, or NCBC). In promotion cadres, de-reservation follows a rigorous statutory approval mechanism to protect reserved quotas.

questions.question_english: Does the legal framework of the POCSO Act, 2012 cover offences committed by a minor child against another child, and how is such an offending child dealt with?
options_english: No, minors cannot be prosecuted for any criminal offence under Indian law
Yes, but the offending child is dealt with under the provisions of the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
Yes, and the offending child is tried directly as an adult in the regular Special POCSO Court
No, the parents of the offending child serve the required prison sentence instead
questions.explanation_english: The POCSO Act, 2012 applies to any offence committed against a child, regardless of whether the perpetrator is an adult or another child. However, when an offence under the POCSO Act is alleged to have been committed by a person below the age of 18 years, Section 28(2) and Section 34 of the POCSO Act read with the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act) come into operation. The offending child is classified as a 'Child in Conflict with Law' (CCL). Such an individual cannot be arrested or detained in regular police lockups or adult prisons, nor tried in regular adult criminal courts. Instead, the matter is submitted to the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) constituted under the JJ Act, 2015. The JJB conducts an inquiry with a focus on reform, counseling, and rehabilitation rather than retributive punishment, directing institutional placement in an Observation Home or Special Home if warranted.

questions.question_english: According to the Income Tax Act, 1961, which of the following accurately describes the "Assessment Year" for a salaried government employee?
options_english: The financial year in which income is actually earned by the employee
The period of 12 months commencing on the 1st day of April every year, immediately following the Previous Year
The calendar year in which the employee files their income tax return
The academic session during which the school disburses the salary
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(9) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, 'Assessment Year' (AY) is defined as the period of twelve consecutive months commencing on the 1st day of April every year. The financial year in which an individual earns income is termed the 'Previous Year' (PY) under Section 3. The income earned during the Previous Year is assessed, evaluated, and taxed during the immediately succeeding Assessment Year (for example, income earned during PY 2023–24 is assessed in AY 2024–25). Therefore, the statutory period of 12 months beginning on April 1 following the Previous Year accurately defines the Assessment Year.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 2(9) के तहत, 'कर-निर्धारण वर्ष' (असेसमेंट ईयर) को प्रत्येक वर्ष 1 अप्रैल से शुरू होने वाली 12 महीनों की अवधि के रूप में परिभाषित किया गया है। जिस वित्तीय वर्ष में आय अर्जित की जाती है, उसे धारा 3 के अंतर्गत 'पूर्ववर्ती वर्ष' (प्रीवियस ईयर / वित्तीय वर्ष) कहा जाता है। पूर्ववर्ती वर्ष में अर्जित आय का आकलन और कराधान ठीक उसके बाद आने वाले कर-निर्धारण वर्ष में किया जाता है (उदाहरणार्थ, वित्तीय वर्ष 2023-24 में अर्जित आय का कर निर्धारण वर्ष 2024-25 में होता है)। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.explanation_english: Paragraph 6.3 of DoPT OM No. 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) dated 31st January 2019 explicitly lays down the rule governing unfilled EWS vacancies: "Where in any recruitment year any vacancy earmarked for EWS cannot be filled up due to non availability of a suitable candidate belonging to EWS, such vacancies for that particular recruitment year shall not be carried forward to the next recruitment year as backlog." Instead, such unfilled vacancies are de-reserved in that recruitment cycle itself and filled up by treating them as unreserved (UR) vacancies. Assertion (A): If a school engages a guest speaker for a specialized educational workshop and pays a professional fee of ₹50,000, TDS must be deducted at 10% under Section 194J.
Reason (R): Section 194J governs the deduction of tax at source on fees for professional or technical services.

options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

(A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) provides the direct statutory justification for Assertion (A).

1. Section 194J of the Income Tax Act, 1961 mandates deduction of tax at source on payments made to a resident towards fees for professional or technical services.
2. The threshold limit under Section 194J is ₹30,000 per financial year for each category of service.
3. Since the payment of ₹50,000 to the guest expert/speaker exceeds the statutory limit of ₹30,000, tax must be deducted at source at the standard rate of 10% (for professional services).
4. Reason (R) correctly explains that Section 194J is the governing provision for tax deduction on fees for professional services, thereby directly explaining Assertion (A).

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 51 of the CGST Act, 2017 read with Rule 66 of the CGST Rules, 2017, every entity required to deduct tax at source (TDS deductors, including government departments and local authorities) must file a monthly return in Form GSTR-7 electronically on the common GST portal. It reports details of TDS deducted, tax deposited, and supplier GSTINs, which auto-populates in the suppliers' electronic cash ledger. In contrast, GSTR-1 is for outward supplies, GSTR-3B is the monthly summary return, and GSTR-9 is the annual return.

As per the Central Government rules governing EWS reservation (DoPT OM No. 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) dated 31.01.2019), the term 'income' is defined comprehensively:

1. Gross Annual Income: It refers to gross income (prior to tax deductions, provident fund deductions, or other personal deductions), NOT take-home or net salary.
2. All Sources Included: The income calculation encompasses earnings from all sources, including salary, agriculture, business, profession, and other income streams. Agricultural income is expressly included.
3. Relevant Timeframe: Income is evaluated for the 'financial year prior to the year of application' for the certificate (e.g., for an application made in 2024-25, the income of FY 2023-24 is assessed).
4. Aggregation of Family: The combined income of the candidate, their parents, spouse, siblings under 18, and children under 18 must be computed together.

questions.question_english: In the event of a conflict between a law made by the Parliament and a law made by the State Legislature of Delhi on a matter concerning school education (a subject in the Concurrent List), which of the following principles will apply?
options_english: The State law will automatically prevail within the territorial jurisdiction of Delhi.
Both laws will be struck down and declared completely void by the Supreme Court.
The Parliamentary law prevails under Article 254.
The matter will be referred to a specially constituted Joint Committee of Parliament.
questions.explanation_english: Article 254 of the Constitution establishes the principle of federal supremacy regarding Concurrent List subjects. questions.explanation_english: Under Section 17(2) of the CGST Act, 2017, where goods or services are used by a registered person partly for effecting taxable supplies and partly for effecting exempt supplies, the amount of credit is restricted to so much of the input tax as is attributable to taxable supplies.
